analysis:
This batch changes only test files: the new ServingReadinessTests.swift (head lines 1-191) and added suites in ProviderAuthorizationConnectionTests.swift (head lines 41-186). No production code is visible, so there is no direct change to security controls. The tests cover the following behavior:
- ServingReadiness.verdict maps coordinator authorization reasons to operator advice. It treats authorization path none, an expired App Attest lease, or an untrusted status as blocked, and a legacy or hardware path as authorized. A self_signed label with no authorization object yields no verdict, which is consistent with T-052 (a legacy label is not serving permission).
- UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery implements idle-only re-registration with threshold, jitter and backoff (30 min up to 4 h). The tests show re-registration deferred while an accepted Autopilot command is in flight.
- The tests use test-only ProviderLoop hooks (setUnauthorizedReconnectJitterForTesting, setAutopilotCommandForTesting, installAuthorizationStateFileForTesting) in a private extension in the test target. These do not expand production attack surface.

Relevant threat IDs are T-053, T-057, T-052 and TB-011. The tests confirm that a reconnect clears prior authorization (clearConnectionAuthorization). The supervision logic does not itself grant authorization; re-registration only forces a fresh coordinator decision, so it does not weaken the T-053 binding. Diagnostic advice is local and is not trust evidence.

Open integration questions, outside the supplied evidence:
- Whether the production superviseServingAuthorization, noteCoordinatorConnection and UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery code, and the DaemonState.coordinatorConnection state-file fields, expose sensitive data. The state file is local, and sessionID and machineID are already present.
- Whether the reconnect loop can be abused by a coordinator or provider to cause availability issues. Backoff is capped and gated on idle, per the tests.

No finding is supportable from test-only changes.
